title: Retrospective MRI Analysis of Olfactory Bulb Enlargement in Pediatric Patients with Hydrocephalus.
summary:
Background:
In children with a condition called hydrocephalus (“water on the brain”), too much fluid accumulates inside the head. This can cause certain parts of the brain to enlarge. The olfactory bulb, a small brain structure responsible for the sense of smell, may also change when there is excess fluid in the brain. So far, this possible connection has hardly been studied in humans.

Research Question:
This study aims to find out whether the olfactory bulb becomes enlarged in children with hydrocephalus and whether this enlargement decreases again after treatment that relieves the excess fluid.

Methods:
The study will analyze existing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans from children who were diagnosed with hydrocephalus between 2018 and 2025. No new medical procedures will be performed. The MRI images will be reviewed retrospectively to measure possible changes in the olfactory bulb and to compare them with the size of the brain’s fluid spaces. All data will be handled in a strictly confidential and anonymized manner, so that no conclusions can be drawn about individual patients.
conditions: Analysis of the enlargement of the olfactory bulb cavity (Olfactory Bulb Cavity / Olfactory Bulb Ventricle) in pediatric patients with hydrocephalus.

interventions.name: This retrospective study includes all patients who underwent clinically indicated MRI examinations and were diagnosed with hydrocephalus between 2018 and 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with pre- and post-operative MRI following ventricular shunt placement
Patients with an available thin-slice imaging dataset
Exclusion criteria:
No preoperative imaging available prior to shunt placement
Tumor or other space-occupying lesions, such as hemorrhage
